# pg_improv SQL reference

<!-- Generated by crates/pg_improv/tests/pg-reference.py from a live
     pg_improv; UPDATE_DOCS=1 rewrites it. Do not edit. -->

Every function, setting and status column of pg_improv 0.14.0, read from
the extension's catalog. Every function is in schema `improv` and runs
`SECURITY INVOKER`; a function on a model acts as the model's owner (see
[Privileges](./postgres.md#privileges)). [Improv in Postgres](./postgres.md)
explains how they fit together, and [Compatibility](./compatibility.md)
which of them are stable.

## Functions

### `bind_category`

```sql
improv.bind_category(model text, category text, rel regclass, col text) → void
```

Creates the category if missing and records that `rel.col` supplies its items.

### `bind_measure`

```sql
improv.bind_measure(model text, measure text, rel regclass, value_col text, agg text DEFAULT NULL::text) → void
```

Creates an input measure read from `rel.value_col`. Its dimensions are the categories already bound on `rel`, in category-id order. Two rows on one coordinate are an error unless `agg` (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`) folds them; an aggregated measure is read-only in the GUI.

### `categories`

```sql
improv.categories(model text) → TABLE(id bigint, name text)
```

The model's categories, for a role its policies let open it (`ViewModel`), and for the owner.

### `cells`

```sql
improv.cells(model text, measure text) → TABLE(coord jsonb, value jsonb)
```

The cells of one measure the caller may read (`ReadCell`): an input's from its table, a derived measure's from its result table, read as the owner. A hidden measure answers as one that does not exist.

### `create_model`

```sql
improv.create_model(name text) → bigint
```

Creates the model and its result schema `improv_<lower(name)>`.

### `define`

```sql
improv.define(model text, definition text, replace boolean DEFAULT false) → bigint
```

Adds a derived measure from `Target = expr` and creates its result table, or a named LAMBDA from `Name = LAMBDA(p, …, body)` (see the [README](https://codeberg.org/gregburd/improv/src/branch/main/crates/pg_improv/README.md)). `SQL(...)` and `CALL(...)` are rejected. An existing name is an ERROR unless `replace => true`, which redefines the derived measure (see the [README](https://codeberg.org/gregburd/improv/src/branch/main/crates/pg_improv/README.md)). Returns the measure's (or lambda's) id.

### `drop_measure`

```sql
improv.drop_measure(model text, measure text) → void
```

Drops a measure: a derived one's result table, an input's binding and stored cells, and its catalog row; or a named LAMBDA. An ERROR names the measures (and lambdas) that still reference it.

### `drop_model`

```sql
improv.drop_model(name text) → void
```

Drops the catalog rows, the result schema and the triggers, and takes relations no other logical-mode model binds out of `improv_db`.

### `enable_logical`

```sql
improv.enable_logical(model text) → void
```

Adds the model's bound relations to the database's publication `improv_db` and gives PK-less ones `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL`. Called for you by `bind_measure` and `set_sync_mode(…, 'logical')`. The worker creates the slot.

### `explain_access`

```sql
improv.explain_access(model text, action text, resource jsonb DEFAULT NULL::jsonb, role text DEFAULT NULL::text) → TABLE(step integer, action text, resource text, allowed boolean, policies text[], errors text[])
```

Each question the policy rules ask for `role` (the caller when NULL) doing `action` on `resource` (NULL: the model; `{"measure": M}`, `{"measure": M, "at": {"Category": "Item"}}`, `{"category": C}`, `{"category": C, "item": I}`, `{"view": V}`), with the deciding policies, to the first denial. Only the owner's side and `Admin`s ask about others or see the policies; a role asking about itself gets one row, allowed or not.

### `items`

```sql
improv.items(model text) → TABLE(category text, id bigint, name text)
```

The items the caller may read (`ReadItem`).

### `measures`

```sql
improv.measures(model text) → TABLE(id bigint, name text, kind text, value_type text, categories text[], formula text)
```

The measures the caller may read (`ReadMeasure`); `formula` is NULL unless every measure it reads is readable too.

### `policies`

```sql
improv.policies(model text) → TABLE(version bigint, policies text, groups text, set_by text, set_at timestamp with time zone)
```

The stored policies: no row if never set, a NULL `policies` after a clear. For the owner's side and `Admin`s.

### `recalc` (1 arguments)

```sql
improv.recalc(model text) → bigint
```

Recomputes every derived measure in the caller's transaction and returns the number of result rows inserted, updated or deleted.

### `recalc` (2 arguments)

```sql
improv.recalc(model text, measures text[]) → bigint
```

Recomputes only the named measures (input or derived, case-insensitive) and every derived measure that depends on them. `NULL` means all.

### `set_cells`

```sql
improv.set_cells(model text, edits jsonb) → bigint
```

Sets (`null`: clears) input cells, as `what_if`'s edits name them, writing the bound table (or `improv.cell`) as the owner and recomputing. Each cell must pass `EditCell`; one that does not refuses the call. Returns the cells written. Audited.

### `set_policies`

```sql
improv.set_policies(model text, policies text, groups text DEFAULT NULL::text) → bigint
```

Stores the model's access policies (Cedar text, groups JSON), validated as `improv policy set` validates them; `NULL` policies clears them. Returns the new version. For the owner, a role that may act as it, or one the policies allow `Admin`. Audited. See [Access policies](./postgres.md#access-policies).

### `set_sync_mode`

```sql
improv.set_sync_mode(model text, mode text) → void
```

`trigger`: installs the sync triggers on every bound relation and recomputes once (re-run it after binding a new relation). `commit`: recomputes once, then once per writing transaction before it commits; needs the preload. `logical`/`manual`: removes the triggers.

### `status`

```sql
improv.status(model text) → TABLE(sync_mode text, slot text, lag_bytes bigint, confirmed_lsn text, last_applied_at timestamp with time zone, rows_applied bigint, last_error text, incremental_applies bigint, rebuilds bigint, fold_bytes bigint, engine_bytes bigint)
```

How the model is kept current, how far the logical worker is behind, and how it applied its batches: `incremental_applies` to the live engine, `rebuilds` full loads (the first catch-up, structural changes, and what it could not apply incrementally).

### `sync_publication`

```sql
improv.sync_publication() → void
```

Sets `improv_db` to the union of the relations every logical-mode model binds (creating it when missing). Called for you by every function that changes that set; run it by hand to repair a publication edited by hand.

### `what_if`

```sql
improv.what_if(model text, edits jsonb) → TABLE(measure text, coord jsonb, value jsonb)
```

Evaluates the model with `edits` applied in memory and returns the derived cells that differ from the stored results (`value` NULL: the cell would vanish). Writes nothing. When every edit has the same categories and the measures they feed are element-wise, it loads and compares only the edited coordinates, as trigger mode does. Only a role that may act as the model's owner may call it, and it reads as the owner (see [Privileges](./postgres.md#privileges), which shows how to give it to other roles).

### Internal functions

The extension calls these itself (as triggers, as the `LANGUAGE improv`
handler, or from its row-level security policies). Do not call them.

| Function | Returns | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cell_name(model bigint, measure bigint, dim integer, slot integer)` | text | Row-level security on a result table, under `cell_rule` 2: the `slot`th name of dimension `dim` the caller may not read (NULL past the last). |
| `cell_rule(model bigint, measure bigint)` | integer | Row-level security on a result table of a model with access policies, once per statement (an InitPlan): 0 shows every row, 1 none (the stored policies cannot be used, or nothing of the measure is readable), 2 compares each row's names with `cell_name`'s (only while `improv.stale` vouches that every result row names the model's items), 3 checks each row with `row_visible`. |
| `cell_visible(model bigint, measure bigint, dims text[])` | boolean | Whether the caller may read the cell of `measure` at `dims` (item names in the measure's category order), as the result tables' row-level security decides it: true without policies and for the owner's side; false for a hidden cell, a name the model lacks, and every cell when the stored policies cannot be used. The check of a result table without dimensions. |
| `check_owner()` | trigger | Trigger on `improv.model`: only a role that may act as both the current and the new owner may set or change a model's owner. |
| `commit_capture()` | trigger | Commit mode's row-capture statement trigger (`improv.commit_capture = 'rows'`): notes the coordinates a statement touched for the pre-commit recompute. |
| `commit_catalog_changed()` | trigger | Statement trigger on `improv.model` and `improv.binding`: invalidates every backend's cache of the commit-mode relations. |
| `item_changed()` | trigger | Statement trigger on `improv.item`: an item renamed or deleted marks its model's result rows stale (`improv.stale`), so the result tables' qual checks them row by row until a recalc. |
| `may_act_as(r regrole)` | boolean | Whether the caller may act as role `r`: a superuser, or a member with the right to `SET ROLE` to it (any member on PG 15). The row-level security policies on the catalog call it. |
| `mint_items(p_model bigint, p_cats bigint[], p_names text[])` | TABLE(category_id bigint, name text, id bigint) | Assigns ids to item names it has not seen, in lexical order, never reusing one. Shared with the `postgres://` model store. |
| `on_change()` | trigger | Trigger mode's sync trigger: recomputes the changed inputs' dependents in the writer's transaction, as the model's owner. |
| `plimprov_call_handler()` | language_handler | The `LANGUAGE improv` call handler. |
| `plimprov_validator(oid)` | void | The `LANGUAGE improv` validator: checks the signature, and the body when `check_function_bodies` is on. |
| `result_written()` | trigger | Statement trigger on a filtered result table: a write marks the model's result rows stale (`improv.stale`) until a recalc checks them. |
| `row_visible(model bigint, measure bigint, VARIADIC dims "any")` | boolean | Row-level security on a result table, per row under `cell_rule` 3: `cell_visible`'s answer for the row's dimension values (text, in the measure's category order), from a decision table kept for the query. |
| `unrestricted(model bigint)` | boolean | Row-level security on the catalog: whether the caller may read model `model`'s measures, bindings, views and lambdas. True without access policies (0.12's rule) and for the owner's side. |

## Settings (GUCs)

`Set in` is the GUC's context: where a change takes effect.

| GUC | Type | Default | Range | Set in | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `improv.commit_capture` | enum | `relations` | `relations`, `rows` | any session (`SET`) | What entering commit sync mode installs on the bound tables. relations (the default): nothing, and each COMMIT recomputes the written tables' dependents in full; rows: statement triggers that capture the touched coordinates, so COMMIT recomputes only those. Read by improv.set_sync_mode. |
| `improv.database` | string | `postgres` |  | `postgresql.conf`, restart | Database the pg_improv sync worker connects to. The logical-decoding worker serves the Improv models of this one database. |
| `improv.max_cells` | integer | `5000000` | 0–2147483647 | any session (`SET`) | Maximum bound input cells per Improv model. Every load of a model (recalc, define, a trigger-mode or commit-mode recompute, the sync worker's rebuild and apply) refuses a model with more bound input cells. |
| `improv.max_changes` | integer | `10000` | 1–2147483647 | `postgresql.conf`, reload | Most decoded changes one poll of the sync worker reads. Bounds the work (and memory) of one poll. |
| `improv.max_model_memory` | integer | `0` MB | 0–2147483647 MB | `postgresql.conf`, reload | Most memory (MB) one model's live state may hold in the sync worker. A model whose fold state plus engine (as improv.status estimates them) would exceed it is refused: the worker logs why, sets its last_error, and retries it with backoff instead of growing until the backend is killed; 0 is no cap. |
| `improv.max_slot_lag` | integer | `4096` MB | 0–2147483647 MB | `postgresql.conf`, reload | WAL (MB) the sync worker's slot may lag before it is dropped and remade. Past it the worker drops the slot and rebuilds each model from its tables, rather than retain more WAL; 0 never drops it. A cap that also holds while the worker is down is max_slot_wal_keep_size. |
| `improv.poll_ms` | integer | `200` | 10–60000 | `postgresql.conf`, reload | How often the pg_improv sync worker polls its slot, in ms. Lower is fresher results; higher is fewer idle wakeups. |
| `improv.raise_errors` | bool | `off` |  | any session (`SET`) | Raise a LANGUAGE improv error value instead of returning NULL. When on, a LANGUAGE improv function whose result is an error value (#DIV/0!, #NUM!, #N/A, ...) raises an ERROR naming it; when off it returns NULL. |

`improv.database` exists only when pg_improv is in
`shared_preload_libraries`.

## `improv.status(model)` columns

One row per call; [Monitoring](./monitoring.md) says what a healthy value
looks like and which to alert on.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sync_mode` | text | `logical`, `trigger`, `commit` or `manual`. |
| `slot` | text | `improv_db` in logical mode (the slot every logical model of the database shares); NULL otherwise. |
| `lag_bytes` | bigint | `pg_current_wal_lsn() − confirmed_flush_lsn` of the slot: WAL the worker has not confirmed yet. It is the **slot's** lag, so every logical model of the database shows the same number. NULL when the slot does not exist (not yet created, or dropped). |
| `confirmed_lsn` | text | The slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn`. |
| `last_applied_at` | timestamptz | When the worker last applied a batch to this model, or rebuilt it. It does not move while the model's tables are idle. NULL before the first catch-up, and after a new slot resets progress. |
| `rows_applied` | bigint | Result rows the worker has written for this model (inserted, updated or deleted), in total. |
| `last_error` | text | Why the worker's last attempt at this model failed; NULL after a success. While set, the model is retried with backoff (0.5 s, doubling, up to 60 s), and every retry is a full rebuild. |
| `incremental_applies` | bigint | Batches the worker fed to the live engine (the cheap path). |
| `rebuilds` | bigint | Full reloads and recomputes. The first catch-up counts one; so does each worker restart, structural change (`define`, a new binding), and batch that needs one ([Concepts](./concepts.md#incremental-recalculation) lists the triggers). |
| `fold_bytes` | bigint | Estimated heap of the model's fold state in the worker: what its aggregated bindings (`agg => …`) keep per coordinate. A `count_distinct`, `min` or `max` binding keeps its values too, so it grows with their number. 0 without aggregated bindings. Measured after each rebuild, and at most once a second while the model applies batches; NULL while the worker holds no live state for the model (before its first change, or after it failed). |
| `engine_bytes` | bigint | Estimated heap of the model's live engine and input cells in the worker, as of the same moment. `fold_bytes + engine_bytes` is what [`improv.max_model_memory`](./monitoring.md#capping-a-models-memory) caps. |

## `improv.models` columns

A view of every model, for anyone who may read the catalog.

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | text | The model's name. |
| `owner` | regrole | The role the model reads its tables and writes its results as. |
| `sync_mode` | text | `logical`, `trigger`, `commit` or `manual`. |
| `may_change` | boolean | Whether the caller may act as the owner: change the model, read its items and cells, `what_if` it. |
| `result_schema` | text | The schema of its result tables, `improv_<lower(name)>`. |
